sections.summary: The law should back community admins with guidelines and safe harbours, and empowers the OSC to issue Right-of-Reply Directions, reduce amplification and award enhanced damages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Most community admins want safe spaces, the law should back them up with guidelines and safe harbours for good faith action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It empowers the OSC to issue Right-of-Reply Directions, Reduce Engagement or amplification and award enhanced damages for persistent offenders – strong but calibrated safeguards for each type of online harm.

sections.label: Platforms assessing risks before harm
sections.summary: Other jurisdictions now require major platforms to assess and mitigate certain risks before harm occurs, especially for children and vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Other jurisdictions now require major platforms to assess and mitigate certain risks before harm occurs, especially for children and vulnerable groups.

sections.label: Content generating intermediaries online safety
sections.summary: The passage says unchecked content can put children and vulnerable users at risk and suggests considering prescribing content generating intermediaries with content moderation, age assurance and transparency obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Left unchecked, this can put children and vulnerable users at risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We should consider whether "content generating intermediaries" should be prescribed under our online safety framework with clear obligations on content moderation, age assurance and transparency.

sections.label: Raising OSC action threshold
sections.summary: The passage states that raising the OSC action threshold from reason to suspect to reasonable grounds to believe would raise barriers for victims and delay timely relief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Raising the threshold for OSC action from "reason to suspect" to "reasonable grounds to believe" would raise barriers for victims and delay timely relief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Waiting for victims to produce evidence of reasonable grounds to believe before acting is not protection.

sections.label: UK Online Safety Act comparison
sections.summary: The passage states the UK Online Safety Act uses reasonable grounds to believe for regulated services, duty of care and final enforcement, but not victim redress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The UK Online Safety Act does use the reasonable grounds to believe in specific context, such as when defining the scope of regulated services, when defining the platform's duty of care, and for final enforcement, but I believe not to victim redress, which happens at the platform level, so it is not equivalent to the OSC stepping in to issue, takedown or redress orders.

sections.label: Removing finality clauses appeals
sections.summary: The passage states that removing finality clauses from appeals provisions and adding a right to appeal OSC cases to the High Court could turn quick relief into long and costly litigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Removing the finality clauses from the appeals provisions and adding a right to appeal OSC cases to the High Court could turn quick relief into long and costly litigation.

sections.label: Swift recourse for online harms
sections.summary: The passage states she yearns for effective enforcement action to stop perpetrators quickly and decisively, reflecting the Government's commitment to swift recourse for victims of online harms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: She yearns for effective enforcement action that can stop the perpetrator quickly and decisively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It reflects the Government’s commitment towards providing swift and decisive recourse to victims of online harms.

sections.label: Adequacy of OSC penalties
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister whether prescribed penalties of a fine up to $20,000 and jail not exceeding 12 months for failing to comply with OSC's direction are adequate as a deterrent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, given the severe mental and emotional distress online harms have caused, I would like to ask Minister whether the prescribed penalties of a fine of up to $20,000 and a jail term not exceeding 12 months for the failure to comply with OSC’s direction is adequate to serve as a deterrent to stop the offending actions promptly.

sections.label: Extraterritorial offences and OSC enforcement
sections.summary: Clause 78 would let courts deal with offences committed outside Singapore, contingent on the OSC detecting wrongdoing and getting overseas wrongdoers to comply or be apprehended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Clause 78 would empower our courts legally to deal with offences under the Bill which are committed outside Singapore, but the courts’ ability to deal with such offences would be contingent on the OSC’s efficacy in detecting the wrongdoing, getting the wrongdoers who are located overseas to comply with the directives and apprehending them if they do not.

sections.label: SG Nasi Lemak chatgroup membership
sections.summary: The SG Nasi Lemak Telegram chatgroup had more than 44,000 members at its peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Members of this House will know that SG Nasi Lemak Telegram chatgroup at its peak had more than 44,000 members.

sections.label: OSC resources, powers and reporting
sections.summary: The speaker asks how MDDI will resource the OSC, whether it needs enhanced powers, and opposes annual reporting to Parliament at this phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How will MDDI ensure that OSC will be endowed with sufficient resources to meet its core mission?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Also, has MDDI considered if OSC’s officers will require enhanced powers, including possibly such as those under the Criminal Procedure Code to be more effective in its investigation and enforcement?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And in this starting phase, my view is that its focus should be on getting its effectiveness on the ground to stop cases of online harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is also why, while I understand WP's proposal for annual reporting to Parliament, I am not supportive of the proposed amendment to this effect at this point, given the administrative load it will add to the OSC in its current phase of development.

sections.label: Clarifying presumption of guilt
sections.summary: The speaker seeks confirmation on a statement about proof of guilt and clarifies that the Commissioner's prescribed order does not presume guilt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Sorry, just to confirm, did you say a person cannot be proven guilty until proven innocent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: I would just like to clarify that I do not think the order that is prescribed by the Commissioner presumes guilt.

sections.label: Safeguards against false victim information
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill has strong safeguards because false information submitted to the Commissioner by a purported victim will be dealt with in the Courts with severe punishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Foo, would you like to respond to Ms Chong?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: I wanted to clarify that, indeed, and this is why I mentioned that there are strong safeguards within the current framework of the Bill, because if it is indeed found that the purported victim had submitted false information to the Commissioner, that matter will be dealt with in the Courts and the punishments are severe.

sections.label: Thresholds for online harm tests
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies that 'reason to suspect' and 'reasonable grounds to believe' are established subjective and objective legal tests, and the objective test was chosen to avoid online harm cases with no clear parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: Yes, my clarification for Mr Foo is, essentially, "reason to suspect" and "reasonable grounds to believe", the two thresholds that we are discussing and we have proposed in our amendment, these are well established legal tests: one is a subjective test and one is an objective test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: And the reason we have, on balance, decided that the objective test is better is precisely to avoid situations where you have online harms where, basically, no parties are angels – he said, she said, we said, they said.

sections.label: Online harm survey findings
sections.summary: A 2025 MDDI survey found one in three Singaporeans faced online harm and two in five victims reported serious emotional distress.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A 2025 survey by MDDI found that one in three Singaporeans had faced online harm and two in five victims reported serious emotional distress.

sections.label: Bill establishes OSC
sections.summary: The Bill establishes the OSC to give victims a faster and more direct path to help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Bill establishes the OSC to give victims a faster and more direct path to help.

sections.label: Mystery shopper test results
sections.summary: MDDI's mystery shopper tests found more than half of valid reports of serious content were ignored or delayed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The MDDI's mystery shopper tests found that more than half of valid reports of serious content were ignored or delayed.

sections.label: Community-care worker abuse survey
sections.summary: In May 2025, the Ministry of Health reported nearly two-thirds of community-care workers had witnessed or experienced abuse or harassment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In May 2025, the Ministry of Health reported that nearly two-thirds of community-care workers had witnessed or experienced abuse or harassment.

sections.label: Platforms as first responders
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government will ensure platforms remain first responders after the Commission is activated, so they cannot delay or defer action.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will the Government ensure that platforms remain first responders even after the Commission is activated, so that they cannot delay or defer action?

sections.label: Personal data protection when unmasking
sections.summary: The question asks how personal data will be protected even as perpetrators are unmasked.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will personal data be protected even as perpetrators are unmasked?

sections.label: Guidance for frontline staff
sections.summary: Asks whether Ministries will develop practical guidance for schools, hospitals and community agencies staff to activate protections and respond with empathy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Given that schools, hospitals and community agencies are often the first to encounter online-related distress, will the relevant Ministries consider developing practical guidance to help staff activate these protections and respond with empathy?

sections.label: Unions acting for members
sections.summary: Asks what process will let unions or professional associations act swiftly on behalf of their members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What will be the process for unions or professional associations to act swiftly on behalf of their members?

sections.label: Relief, duties and civil rights
sections.summary: States the Bill gives victims new avenues of relief through the Commissioner of Online Safety, imposes duties on online service providers and creates civil rights of action.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Specifically, it gives victims of online harms, new avenues of relief through the Commissioner of Online Safety, impose clear duties on online service providers, and creates civil rights of action for victims.

sections.label: Timeliness of response standards
sections.summary: Notes clause 23 lets victims report alleged online harmful activity, but the Bill does not prescribe what counts as a timely response.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On service standards, clause 23 in Part 4 enables victims to make a report of alleged online harmful activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But while the Bill mentions that it aims to provide a timely means of redress, it does not yet prescribe what counts as a timely response.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The point here is this: online harm spreads by hours, not by weeks or months.

sections.label: Statutory torts for victims
sections.summary: States the Bill introduces statutory torts giving victims the right to bring civil proceedings for defined harms such as intimate image abuse and child abuse imagery.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces statutory torts, which gives victims the right to bring civil proceedings for defined harms such as intimate image abuse, child abuse imagery and so on.

sections.label: Reliefs, remedies and non-monetary losses
sections.summary: Notes Parts 5 and 13 provide reliefs and remedies such as content removal, account restrictions and compensation, and seeks clarification on non-monetary losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Part 5 of the Bill on the directions and orders of the Commissioner, as well as Part 13 of the Bill on Damages and Remedies provide various reliefs and remedies to victims of online harms such as removal of content, account restrictions and compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, I would like to seek clarification on whether non-monetary losses could also be considered within this Bill framework.

sections.label: Upstream prevention and platform design
sections.summary: The Bill defines serious harms clearly, but major online platforms should also prioritise user safety and privacy-by-design features.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Deterrence after harm is necessary, but prevention of online harms upstream is better.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill defines serious harms clearly, but we should also work to ensure that major online platforms operating here continue to prioritise user safety and privacy-by-design principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: These include features: (a) age-appropriate design; (b) high-privacy default settings applied for minors; and (c) safer recommender settings for young users.

sections.label: Criminal law amendments penalties
sections.summary: The Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act passed yesterday provided enhanced penalties for many of the same online harms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: It was opportune that we debated and passed the Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: That Bill provided enhanced penalties under our criminal laws for many of the same online harms that are the subject of this Bill.

sections.label: MDDI survey online harm prevalence
sections.summary: MDDI's survey found one-third of respondents experienced online harm in the past year, suggesting hundreds of thousands of reportable harms yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: MDDI's survey has found that one-third of respondents experienced online harm in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: We have more than three million Singaporeans alone in our population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And so, if the MDDI survey is representative of the general population, we could well be looking at hundreds of thousands of potentially reportable online harms every year.

sections.label: No definitive OSC performance guidelines
sections.summary: The speaker concluded it may be better not to impose definitive performance guidelines on OSC at this stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: On service levels, report to relief times and having clear guidelines and standards at the outset, especially given the Australians' experience with operationalising their eSafety Commission, I, myself, have thought about this issue a fair bit and I have come to the conclusion that it may be better for us to not impose definitive performance guidelines on OSC at this stage, as we are building it up.

sections.label: Time and space for OSC
sections.summary: OSC has few precedents and must create its own playbook, so it should be given time and space to build up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Because as what the Minister alluded to, we have very few precedents to refer to and OSC has to pretty much create its own playbook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, the best way to set OSC up for success, borrowing the hon Member, Mr Sharael Taha's words, "the best way to set it up for success is to give it the time and space to build itself up properly." In the meantime, like I said, let us trust that the Government will go about implementing OSC with the same verve and in the same thoughtful, thorough, yet calibrated and pragmatic manner that it has architected our laws to secure the online commons.

sections.label: Online harms and victim help
sections.summary: The Bill gives victims faster, cheaper routes to seek help and holds platforms more responsible for safe spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Online harms – whether harassment, doxxing or intimate-image abuse – can follow a child home long after the device is switched off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill gives victims faster, cheaper routes to seek help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It also holds platforms more responsible for keeping their spaces safe.

sections.label: Australia Online Safety Act
sections.summary: The Australia Online Safety Act requires platforms to comply with removal notices relating to children within 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, the Australia Online Safety Act requires platforms to comply with removal notices relating to children within 24 hours.

sections.label: Commission workflows and benchmarks
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Commission will provide clear workflows and templates, set service benchmarks, and offer capacity-building support for smaller platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To keep the playing field level, I hope the Commission will provide clear workflows and templates for reporting and response; set service benchmarks on how quickly cases are acknowledged, investigated and resolved; and offer capacity-building support, such as training, reporting templates or open-source moderation tools, for smaller platforms to plug into.

sections.label: OSC responsibilities and benchmarks
sections.summary: OSC will handle victim reports, issue directions to platforms and coordinate with law enforcement, and should publish clear service benchmarks publicly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: OSC will carry heavy responsibilities – from handling victim reports to issuing directions to platforms and coordinating with law enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To build public confidence, OSC should not only set but publish clear service benchmarks publicly, on how quickly cases are acknowledged, investigated and resolved.

sections.label: Internet as digital campus
sections.summary: The Internet should be a place to communicate, learn and grow with peace of mind, and this Bill helps victims obtain relief and requires platforms to take responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Internet is like our digital campus and should be a place where people can communicate, learn and grow with peace of mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill can help the victims obtain relief more quickly and requires online platforms to take responsibility.

sections.label: OSC resources for smaller platforms
sections.summary: The OSC should have sufficient resources and capabilities to assist small- and medium-sized platforms improve content control standards, and the speaker supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Third, ensure that the OSC has sufficient resources and capabilities to assist small- and medium-sized platforms to improve their content control standards. : Sir, in conclusion, I support this Bill because it protects our people, strengthens accountability and encourages a healthier digital culture.

sections.label: OSC action against abusive users
sections.summary: The Bill will empower the newly established OSC to take action against users who abuse the Internet to harm others.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill will empower the newly established OSC to take action against users who abuse the Internet to harm others.

sections.label: Online Safety Commissioner enforcement scope
sections.summary: The OSC will start with five of 13 online harm types: online harassment, doxxing, online stalking, intimate image abuse and image-based child abuse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They will provide victims the legal basis to seek accountability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I understand that enforcement will require significant resources and hence, the OSC will start with five of the 13 types of online harms, focusing on online harassment, doxxing, online stalking, intimate image abuse and image-based child abuse.

sections.label: Penalties and harmful content survey
sections.summary: The Bill sets fines and jail terms for non-compliance, and a survey found over four in five residents encountered harmful online content.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, individuals may be fined up to $20,000 and jailed for up to 12 months, while entities may be fined up to $500,000 for failing to comply with the OSC’s orders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministries to consider increasing the caps for the fines and jail terms and include caning, to empower judges to have more discretion for particularly egregious crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A recent survey by MDDI found that in the past year, more than four in five Singapore residents encountered harmful online content across platforms, like Facebook, Youtube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Reddit, Telegram and WhatsApp.

sections.label: Survey on online harms severity
sections.summary: An IPS survey found non-consensual intimate images seen as most severe, and an IMDA report found platforms often took five days or more to act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: An Institute of Policy Studies survey found that sexual content depicting voyeuristic or intimate images recorded without consent was overwhelmingly perceived as the most severe of online harms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The current reality, as an IMDA report revealed, is that major platforms often took five days or more to act appropriately on user reports of harmful content.

sections.label: Commissioner investigative process clarification
sections.summary: The member seeks clarification on the Commissioner's investigative process, including advisory guidelines on timelines and urgent investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I understand that it will take time and extensive consultations, after the appointment of the Commissioner and other relevant office holders, to formulate the detailed rules governing how the Commissioner may exercise investigative powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek clarification on the Commissioner's investigative process, specifically on the following questions: Will the Commissioner publish advisory guidelines indicating the expected timelines for the investigation and resolution of a complaint, with processes put in place for urgent investigations to take place?

sections.label: Online service provider obligations
sections.summary: Part 12 of the Bill requires online service providers to respond to reports of certain harmful content, with potential tortious liability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Part 12 of the Bill imposes obligations on online service providers to respond to reports against certain harmful content in a timely and adequate manner, with the potential for tortious liability if they fail to do so.

sections.label: Warning systems for harmful content
sections.summary: The member asks whether the Government would require online service providers to implement warning systems for potentially harmful content.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To ensure that such Singaporeans do not fall through the gaps, may I ask the Minister whether the Government would consider requiring online service providers to implement warning systems for potentially harmful content?

sections.label: Strict liability for online offences
sections.summary: Asks whether strict liability is being considered for certain offences under the Bill to strengthen deterrence and protect the public, especially young children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is critical that we create a safe online environment for our young.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether we are considering to introducing strict liability for certain classes of offences under the Bill, to strengthen deterrence and provide stronger protection for the public, especially our young children?

sections.label: Working with transnational stakeholders
sections.summary: Asks how the Government intends to work with entities and individuals beyond Singapore's borders, given Parts 5 and 6 require their cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that Parts 5 and 6 of the Bill will require the cooperation of entities and individuals beyond our borders, I would like to ask the Minister how will the Government currently intend to work with these transnational stakeholders?

sections.label: OSC establishment by 2026
sections.summary: States that establishing the OSC by the first half of 2026 shows the Government's commitment to protecting Singaporeans in increasingly digital lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The establishment of the OSC by the first half of 2026 demonstrates the Government's commitment to protecting Singaporeans in our increasingly digital lives.

sections.label: Online harms categories and case load
sections.summary: Asks for the estimated case load for the Commissioner's Office and Appeal Panel and how resourcing will scale, given 13 categories of online harms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Commission will also seek to handle reports across 13 categories of online harms, with a phased approach implementing five categories by mid-2026 and others following progressively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share what is the estimated case load expected for the new Commissioner's Office and Appeal Panel, and how resourcing will scale with time?

sections.label: Commissioner and Police investigations
sections.summary: Asks how the Commissioner's actions and investigations will coordinate with possible Police investigations into criminal offences arising from the same online activity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How will the Commissioner's actions and investigations coordinate with possible Police investigations into potential criminal offences arising from the same online activity?

sections.label: Codes of practice for online safety
sections.summary: States that the Code of Practice for Online Safety covers six designated social media services and the new Code of Practice for App Distribution Services takes effect 31 March 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Today, the Code of Practice for Online Safety covers six designated social media services and the new Code of Practice for App Distribution Services, effective 31 March 2025 and introduces important age assurance measures.

sections.label: Extending safeguards to gaming and AI
sections.summary: The passage asks whether privacy safeguards and age assurance should extend to gaming platforms, messaging apps, generative AI services and chatbots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would we consider extending privacy safeguards and age assurance to gaming platforms, messaging apps and other services where young people gather by requiring these platforms to implement similar protective features such as disabling unwanted messages, restricting profile viewing, disabling location sharing, and empowering parents to guide the content their children access?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Furthermore, as our young people increasingly engage with generative AI services and chatbots, I hope we might consider whether age assurance and safety features should extend to these emerging technologies.

sections.label: Commission powers and coordination
sections.summary: The passage calls for the Commission to have teeth, resources, clarity on legal pathways, guidance, international cooperation, oversight, inter-agency coordination, platform responses and child protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Let us ensure that this Commission has the teeth, resources, and clarity to deliver justice by providing clarity on how legal pathways work together, guidance that helps everyone understand proportionality, robust international cooperation, adequate resourcing, appropriate oversight, seamless inter-agency coordination, balanced platform responses and comprehensive protection for children.

sections.label: Government response to WP amendments
sections.summary: The Government thanks the WP for amendments it considered seriously, saying OSRA balances swift protection for vulnerable victims with accountability through reconsideration and appeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We thank the WP for proposing the amendments, which we have considered seriously, because we share the common goal of helping victims of online harms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We think OSRA strikes the right balance as it stands, between swift protection for vulnerable victims with sufficient accountability through reconsideration and appeal.

sections.label: Emerging online harms in Singapore
sections.summary: Research and surveys on online harms in Singapore identify emerging issues such as deepfakes and cancel campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: From the research and surveys on online harms in Singapore, we know of emerging issues like inauthentic material abuse, also known as "deepfakes" and online instigation of disproportionate harm, or "cancel campaigns".

sections.label: OSC coordination with agencies
sections.summary: The OSC will work closely with other agencies, including the Police, for backend coordination and to minimise multiple reports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The OSC will work closely with other agencies, including the Police, to ensure backend coordination and minimise the need for multiple reports.

sections.label: IMDA directions under Broadcasting Act
sections.summary: Under the Broadcasting Act, IMDA can issue directions to platforms to disable Singapore users' access to egregious content on online communication services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Under the Broadcasting Act today, the IMDA would already be able to issue directions to platforms to disable Singapore users' access to egregious content on online communication services, such as social media services and app stores.

sections.label: OSC comment reasonableness consideration
sections.summary: Clause 27 lets the OSC consider whether a comment was reasonable and the circumstances it was made in before issuing a direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Specifically, clause 27 states that the OSC can consider whether the comment was reasonable and the circumstances the comment was made in deciding whether OSC should issue a direction.

sections.label: Private information and OSC reports
sections.summary: Private information is not widely available to the public, and a person can report non-consensual disclosure to the OSC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Private information refers to information about a person that is not widely available to the public at large, as explained in Handout 4 that Members received earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We believe as a matter of principle that generally everyone in Singapore should be protected against having their private information shared publicly without consent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Hence, if such information was not public before and disclosed without consent, the person can file a report to the OSC.

sections.label: Right-of-Reply Direction for reputation harm
sections.summary: For publication of a statement harmful to reputation, the Commissioner may only issue a Right-of-Reply Direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For the harm of "publication of statement harmful to reputation", the only direction that may be issued by the Commissioner is a Right-of-Reply Direction.

sections.label: OSC officer communications training
sections.summary: OSC officers will be trained in communications and victim management so each case is handled sensitively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: OSC officers will be trained in communications and victim management to ensure that each case is handled sensitively.

sections.label: OSC caseload and resourcing
sections.summary: Members asked about OSC's expected caseload and resourcing; the initial caseload is estimated to be high, based on factors including Australia's eSafety caseload adjusted for Singapore's population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Ms Elysa Chen, Mr Foo Cexiang, Mr Sharael Taha, Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr David Hoe asked about the expected case load of OSC, and how it will be adequately resourced to provide effective and timely redress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We estimate the initial caseload of OSC to be high, based on various factors, including Australia's eSafety caseload for similar harms, adjusted for Singapore's population.

sections.label: Commissioner's power excludes device seizure
sections.summary: In reply to Mr Pritam Singh, the Commissioner's power would not extend to seizure of devices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: To Mr Pritam Singh's question, the Commissioner's power would not extend to the seizure of devices.

sections.label: OSC focus on severe harms
sections.summary: OSC will focus first on addressing the most severe and prevalent harms, such as online harassment and intimate image abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For a start, OSC will focus efforts on addressing the most severe and prevalent harms, such as online harassment and intimate image abuse.

sections.label: Who can file reports
sections.summary: Victims can report themselves or authorise another individual or entity, and unions and professional bodies can file reports with written authorisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Generally, victims have two options: they can submit a report on their own; or authorise another individual or entity to do so on their behalf.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: To Dr Wan Rizal's question, unions and professional bodies can file reports to OSC if they obtain written authorisation from their member who suffered the specified online harm.

sections.label: Dismissing trivial reports
sections.summary: OSC will have mechanisms to filter out and dismiss trivial, frivolous or vexatious reports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: OSC will have mechanisms in place to filter out and dismiss trivial, frivolous or vexatious reports.

sections.label: Reporting after platform inaction
sections.summary: Where platforms fail to act on online harms within 24 hours, victims can then file a report to the OSC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Where platforms fail to act on online harms within 24 hours, victims can then file a report to the OSC.

sections.label: Shorter timelines for severe harms
sections.summary: The OSC's response time and compliance timeline to a direction will likely be shorter for more severe harms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The OSC's response time and corresponding compliance timeline to a direction, will likely be shorter for more severe harms.

sections.label: Online service providers under OSRA
sections.summary: Under the OSRA Bill, online service providers would include social media services and online messaging services such as WhatsApp, Telegram and WeChat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Under the OSRA Bill, online service providers would include social media services and online messaging services, such as WhatsApp, Telegram and WeChat.

sections.label: OSC directions and non-compliance measures
sections.summary: OSC directions apply to all communicators regardless of location, and non-compliance can lead to geo-blocking, access blocking or app removal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As mentioned, the OSC's directions apply to all communicators, administrators or platforms, regardless of where they are based.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Where Access Disabling Directions are issued to overseas platforms, the platform will be required to geo-block the content to prevent Singapore end-users from accessing it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Further, in such cases of non-compliance, the OSC is empowered to take escalatory measures to require providers of Internet access services to block access to non-compliant online services and online locations or to require providers of app distribution services to remove non-compliant apps from their app stores.

sections.label: Online Harmful Activity Remedial Initiative
sections.summary: The Commissioner may put in place an Online Harmful Activity Remedial Initiative consisting of volunteer programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As shared in my opening speech, the Commissioner may put in place an Online Harmful Activity Remedial Initiative, which consists of the completion of volunteer programmes.

sections.label: SHECARES@SCWO support centre
sections.summary: SHECARES@SCWO is an online harms support centre providing counselling services and legal assistance if needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: SHECARES@SCWO is an online harms support centre that provides counselling services and legal assistance if needed.

sections.label: Public education and outreach
sections.summary: Beyond legislative measures, public education and outreach will be improved to make online safety resources more accessible, practical and action oriented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Beyond legislative measures, we will improve public education and outreach to make online safety resources more accessible, practical and action oriented.

sections.label: OSC agency and private remedy framework
sections.summary: The OSC is an independent agency granting quick directions on platforms, complemented by a private remedy framework of statutory torts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The OSC is set up as an independent agency to provide quick relief and can grant directions quickly in respect of platforms, something that, today, if you wanted to do with the platforms directly, you almost certainly would find that you have a huge hurdle to scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, we provide, in complementary to that, a private remedy framework by way of the statutory torts.

sections.label: Low-barrier accessible remedies framework
sections.summary: The Bill creates a low-barrier and accessible framework for victims to obtain remedies, as these tools do not exist today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is important to remember that we do not have any of these tools today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And this Bill, therefore, in my view, will create a low-barrier and accessible framework for victims to obtain remedies.

sections.label: No criminal liability for online harm
sections.summary: There is no criminal offence, liability or punishment for the online harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, I think Members will know that there is no criminal offence or liability or criminal punishment for the online harm.

sections.label: Compensatory liability under Statutory Torts Framework
sections.summary: Liability under the Statutory Torts Framework is largely compensatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Third, by and large, liability under the Statutory Torts Framework is compensatory.

sections.label: Platform liability conditional on proper notice
sections.summary: Platform liability is conditional on platforms receiving proper notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Fourth, liability for platforms is conditional on them receiving proper notice.

sections.label: Reasonable formula for disabling access
sections.summary: The formula is "reasonable" because access can sometimes be disabled with a flip of the switch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh made the point about what is reasonable, and I think the hon Member talked about an illustration and asked whether "prompt" means it must be forthwith and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have put the formula as "reasonable" because in some cases, you can simply disable access with a flip of the switch.

sections.label: Small Claims Tribunal tortious claims
sections.summary: The speaker is not persuaded the Small Claims Tribunal is set up to investigate and hear tortious claims like this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In a similar way, Ms Lee Hui Ying made the same point and talked about the Small Claims Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I am not immediately currently persuaded that the Small Claims Tribunal is set up to investigate and hear tortious claims like this.

sections.label: Damages for distress and humiliation
sections.summary: Claimants are not limited to monetary compensation, and the Bill empowers the court to grant just and equitable damages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The claimants are not limited to monetary compensation and indeed, many of the harms that is contemplated in this Bill, whether it is harassment or intimate image abuse, they lead to distress and humiliation, and the Bill does empower the court to grant damages as it thinks just and equitable.

sections.label: Remedies under OSRA and POHA
sections.summary: Remedies against administrators and platforms for harms will be provided under OSRA, and POHA statutory torts were not subsumed under OSRA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I made the point in my opening speech that we will provide for remedies against the administrator and the platforms for these harms under OSRA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We did consider, but ultimately, decided not to subsume the POHA statutory torts under OSRA.

sections.label: OSC and Court decisions
sections.summary: The decisions of the OSC and the Court will not bind the other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The decisions of the OSC and the Court will not bind the other.

sections.label: Right-of-Reply and defamation proceedings
sections.summary: Victims can pursue either or both remedies, and a Right-of-Reply Direction is not a prerequisite before commencing defamation court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Instead, many of them want to set the record straight as quickly as possible before their reputation is further harmed, and that is where the Right-of-Reply mechanism meets this need, and victims can choose to pursue either or both remedies, and I would say that it is not a prerequisite to seek a Right-of-Reply Direction first before commencing court proceedings for defamation.

sections.label: PDPA and OSC directions
sections.summary: PDPA obligations do not prevent platforms from complying with the OSC's directions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The short point is that the obligations imposed by the PDPA do not prevent platforms from complying with the OSC's directions.

sections.label: Balance for redressing victim harm
sections.summary: Information may be subject to conditions with penal consequences for misuse, and this overall provides the right balance to redress the victim's harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the other hand, you are getting information that might be subject to conditions and there are also consequences, some of which are penal in nature if you misuse it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we believe overall that this provides the right balance to redress the victim's harm, provide an avenue to pursue the action.

sections.label: Requiring platforms after online harm
sections.summary: Taking into account the balance, platforms will be required to do so once the online harm is established.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Taking into account, as I said earlier, that balance, we decided that we will require the platforms to do so once we have established the online harm.

sections.label: Clause 4 Government exclusion, defamation reply
sections.summary: Clause 4 excludes the Government from the legislation, and the reply addresses victims' quick replies and the OIDH threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In clause 4, Mr Low will be aware that neither the Government will be bound by this legislation nor can the Government avail itself of this legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, on that basis, we do not think that it is suitable not to include the Government either way and for the reasons that we set out in the Explanatory Statement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I had made reference to Ms Elysa Chen's speech; and I note that she actually did not ask about how defamation interacts with the harm of publication of statements harmful to reputation and how the OSC would ascertain disproportionality of OIDH.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Instead, my reply actually addresses the general point on how victims can put out a reply quickly to protect their reputation and how it interacts with other laws, and I shared further on the threshold for OIDH.

sections.label: Stakeholder accountability framework
sections.summary: The framework holds all stakeholders, from platforms to perpetrators, accountable for user safety.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our framework will hold all stakeholders accountable – from platforms to perpetrators – for the safety of users.

sections.label: OSC objective assessment of online harms
sections.summary: The OSC takes an objective approach to online harms, and thresholds are not met merely by someone saying they feel offended.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Minister of State Rahayu has explained how the OSC will take an objective approach in assessing online harms.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These thresholds are not met simply because someone says they feel offended by the content, no matter who that someone is.

sections.label: OSC guidelines on decision factors
sections.summary: The OSC will in time publish guidelines on factors it will consider in its decision making.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In time, the OSC will also publish guidelines on factors that it will consider in its decision making.

sections.label: Commissioner consideration, public interest exemption
sections.summary: The Bill provides that the Commissioner may consider it, but a public interest and overriding exemption could shield bad online actors.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In fact, the Bill provides that the Commissioner may consider it.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But making public interest and overriding exemption could inadvertently provide a shield to bad online actors.

sections.label: OSC remit, refinement, monitoring
sections.summary: The OSC has latitude to act quickly and a duty to act responsibly within clear bounds, and will refine its processes and report on progress.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: OSC has both the latitude to act quickly and the duty to act responsibly within clear bounds.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In designing the OSC's remit, we have taken every care to scope it precisely, proportionately and as practicably as we can, so that it fulfils its mission.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: OSC will learn from experience, continually refine its processes and always strive to do better.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It will continue to monitor and report on its progress, refining the system openly as needed.

sections.label: WP withdrawing its amendments
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the WP will consider withdrawing its amendments if it agrees.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If the WP agrees, I hope it will also consider withdrawing its amendments.

sections.label: Broadcasting Act swift recourse
sections.summary: The Broadcasting Act does not allow victims to seek swift recourse, unlike the proposed amendments.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: On Minister of State Rahayu's point that the Broadcasting Act covers the two categories of harmful online activity covered by our proposed amendments, we note that the Broadcasting Act does not allow victims to seek a swift recourse.

sections.label: OSC no-wrong-door policy
sections.summary: The speaker says a no-wrong-door approach is being taken with OSC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The other point I would make is that OSC – we are taking a no-wrong-door approach, no-wrong-door policy with OSC.

sections.label: Clarifying judicial review process
sections.summary: A Member asks if the Minister refers to existing judicial review power or a distinct process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: We will provide more details on the process at a later time." Sir, I just wanted to clarify if Minister of State Rahayu is still referring to the existing statutory power of the Courts to exercise supervisory jurisdiction over executive actions or is this envisaged as a distinct process?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I am referring to the existing power of judicial review.

sections.label: Platform response speed for victims
sections.summary: A Member asks how quick platforms can be expected to respond to victims of online harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In the first case, I am trying to understand from the victim's perspective, how quick can we expect the platforms to respond to victims of online harm?

sections.label: Statutory Tort Framework notice duties
sections.summary: The Statutory Tort Framework prescribes tortious duties for platforms, administrators and communicators triggered from when they get notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The OSC, on the one hand, the Statutory Tort Framework on the other and, bear in mind, that in the Statutory Tort Framework we have now prescribed in the case of platforms, administrators, communicators, tortious duties that are triggered from the time they get notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, unlike in the past where you can get notice and the Member has heard what Minister Josephine said earlier about the requests from individuals being ignored in the case, sometimes five days or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It would not happen here, because the time runs from when they get the notice.

sections.label: Statutory Tort Framework and OSC
sections.summary: Conduct from when platforms receive notice will be scrutinised, and the Statutory Tort Framework complements the OSC framework in making platforms respond to complained harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The conduct from the time they receive notice will be under scrutiny.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And in a way, that Statutory Tort Framework complements the OSC framework in ensuring that the platforms respond, react and do something about the harm that is complained of.

sections.label: New clause on risk assessment
sections.summary: A new clause entitled "Risk Assessment, Reporting, and Accessibility" was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I introduced a new clause entitled "Risk Assessment, Reporting, and Accessibility."

sections.label: New clause E introduced
sections.summary: A new clause E was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I introduced a new clause E.
